○Protein of interest: The expression of your protein/antigen of interest can be linked to specific cellular events. For example, proteins associated with tight junctions may not be highly expressed if cells are not at confluence. This means that if you would like to image these antigens, the cells need to reach confluency on your imaging slide before performing the ICC to ensure antibody labeling. This issue can be overcome by increasing your seeding density when preparing your cells, ensuring that, at the time of fixation, your cells are confluent and can be labeled with your antibody.○Schedule and doubling time: Always take your cells’ doubling time into consideration; it can affect your schedule and any decision to increase or decrease your seeding density for your experiment.
Total BioWave® Pro processing time: ∼53 min

steps.title: Select imaging substrate
steps.instruction: Use glass or optical‑optimized plastic slides for ICC to ensure optimal clarity, correct refractive index, minimal autofluorescence and a uniform flat surface for easy focusing.

steps.title: Apply surface coating if needed
steps.instruction: Test whether the chosen substrate requires a coating for cell adhesion. Start with basic coatings (gelatin, collagen, Poly‑L‑lysine). If cells still do not adhere, use specialized coatings such as Poly D‑Lysine, Poly ornithine, fibronectin, fibrinogen, laminin, vitronectin, tumor‑derived extracellular matrix, or any combination thereof.

steps.title: Seed cells on 8‑well imaging slides
steps.instruction: Seed cells at a density that will give confluency at the time of fixation, taking into account (1) the protein(s) of interest, (2) the experimental schedule, and (3) the cells' doubling time (Abcam, 2024b). Confluency is especially important for antigens such as tight‑junction proteins.

steps.title: Culture cells to desired confluency
steps.instruction: Follow the cell‑culture schedule: thaw and recover cells for 1–2 days; grow to 70–80 % confluency for 2–5 days (cell‑type dependent); trypsinize, count and reseed (≈1–1.5 h); optionally prepare low‑passage frozen stocks (≈1 h, excluding freezing time); seed onto 8‑well slides (≈30 min); allow attachment and growth for a minimum of 16 h (typically overnight) before ICC. Total active hands‑on time for this culture is ~3–4 h; total elapsed time 3–7 days.

steps.title: Fix cells with 2 % PFA
steps.instruction: Fix the cultured cells by incubating with 2 % paraformaldehyde for 10 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Microwave‑assisted ICC processing (BioWave® Pro)
steps.instruction: Process the fixed cells in the BioWave® Pro microwave using the following timed cycles (total microwave run ≈53 min).

substeps.instruction: Rinse slides with HBSS, HBSS:Su, and HBSS:Su:Sap for a cumulative ≈9 min.

steps.title: Mount slides
steps.instruction: Apply Vectashield mounting medium and let it set for 10–15 min.

steps.title: Conventional ICC (alternate protocol)
steps.instruction: If microwave equipment is unavailable, perform standard ICC as follows.

substeps.instruction: Fix cells with 2 % PFA for 10 min.
Incubate primary antibody either 2 h at room temperature or overnight (12–16 h) at 4 °C.
Incubate secondary antibody for 1 h at room temperature.
Stain organelles for ≈30 min (optional live‑stain can be performed prior to fixation).
Perform final washes and mount with Vectashield for ≈15 min.
